title: Introduce lightweight toolchain fuse and dependency rollback batcher
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: CI presubmit latency and flakiness have been steadily increasing due to many small toolchain image pulls and repeated CI restarts caused by transient dependency upgrade failures. This PR introduces two tied changes: 1) a lightweight 'toolchain fuse' artifact that consolidates frequently-used toolchain bits into a single small, cacheable bootstrap image; 2) a 'dependency rollback batcher' that groups transient lockfile/upgrade failures and offers an automated, reversible rollback batch for presubmit blockers. Motivation: reduce cold presubmit time, reduce infra load from many parallel image fetches, and make dependency rollback actionable and low-noise for maintainers. Implementation notes: - Toolchain fuse: build step that composes minimal runtime bits from existing toolchain microimages (node, go, python helpers) into a deterministic tarball + manifest. It is emitted as an artifact to the CI cache with a content-hash key per toolchain-profile. The presubmit runner will prefer the fused artifact when the profile hash matches, falling back to the legacy microimages. - Dep rollback batcher: a small serverless job that listens to CI failure events tagged with the new 'auto-rollback-candidate' annotation. It aggregates failures over a 10 minute window, groups by lockfile diff, and posts a proposed rollback commit (branch + PR template) to the repo. The proposed PR includes a dry-run of the affected presubmit matrix and an explicit revert test step. Safety: rollback PRs are draft by default and require a human approval step; the batcher supports dry-run-only mode and an allowlist for repositories. Rollout plan: feature gated by repo-level flag; start disabled org-wide, enable for redwood/benchmarks and redwood/examples for 2 weeks, then wider rollout after metrics review. Checklist: - [x] design doc and metrics (ENG-4921) - [x] toolchain fuse build and publish - [x] runner fallback and cache-key unit tests - [x] batcher event consumer + grouping tests - [x] e2e smoke in redwood-examples - [x] staged rollout plan committed - [x] documentation for repo owners and ops See also: design doc link: https://linear.app/eng/issue/ENG-4921/toolchain-fuse-and-rollback-batcher and internal playbook: docs/internal/rollback-batcher.md. reviews: Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Nice approach — I like the content-hash key. Question: what's the expected cache-hit rate on first rollout?
Maya Chen (author): Early run on redwood-examples shows ~70% hit rate for stable profiles; benchmarks improved presubmit cold time by ~22% median.
Priya Desai (reviewer): Security review: did we consider SBOM for the fused artifact?
Maya Chen (author): Yes — fuse build emits SBOM.json alongside the artifact; infra validates SBOM on publish.
Ethan Brooks (reviewer): The batcher looks useful but could spam maintainers. Add a debouncing window and draft PRs by default.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented debouncing (10m) and draft-only mode; updated description and tests.
